title: Align metering boundaries and overage credit workflows for enterprise contracts and SQ responses
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines and implements an operational playbook for how Redwood handles metering boundaries, proration, and overage credits for enterprise contracts, and how we answer tightly scoped billing questions in security questionnaires (SQs). The goal is to remove ambiguity between sales/CS/legal, billing ops, and the runtime team so that enterprise customers get predictable invoices and we can automate standard adjustments without manual engineering work for common edge cases.

Context and motivation:
- Multiple enterprise customers have reported inconsistent invoices during mid-cycle contract amendments (seat count changes, reserved capacity downgrades/upgrades) and on legacy trials that convert mid-cycle.
- CS and Sales have requested a single canonical approach we can document in SQs and use to automate adjustments: how we calculate usage windows, how we apply credits for partial months, rounding rules for token counts, how refunds and invoice re-issues are handled, and auditing requirements for KMS/HSM-backed billing metadata.
- Engineering changes (ENG-2764; ENG-2910) touched metering window alignment and prefix caching; we need to agree on business rules before finalizing runtime behavior or we risk billing regressions.

Scope:
- Define canonical "metering boundary" definitions (UTC midnight vs subscription timezone, invoice period alignment for reserved capacity vs hosted usage).
- Standardize proration algorithm for: seat changes, reserved capacity commit changes, and switching between hosted/dedicated models mid-cycle.
- Define overage handling: immediate billing vs crediting on next invoice, soft-threshold smoothing (to reduce noise from bursty traffic), and credit calculation examples.
- Refund & invoice adjustments: when we auto-issue a credit, when we re-issue an invoice, escalation criteria for manual intervention.
- Security questionnaire language: short canonical answers and supporting artifacts (audit logs, KMS key IDs, retention policies for billing evidence).
- Implementation checklist for Billing Ops + Runtime + Console teams, including a migration plan for existing contracts.

Constraints and trade-offs considered:
- Precision vs operational overhead: very granular token-level refunds are accurate but increase support load and can expose confidential prompts. We prefer invoice-level credits with clear traceability back to usage windows unless customer contract demands per-token audit.
- Timezone alignment: aligning to customer local timezone reduces perceived surprises but complicates multi-region routing and KMS audit joins. We propose using UTC for canonical metering and providing localized invoice views in Console only.
- Immediate billing of overages improves cashflow but increases churn risk; default will be credit-on-next-invoice with opt-in immediate invoicing for enterprise customers.

Acceptance criteria:
- A written playbook (this doc) with clear definitions, examples, and decision trees for common cases.
- Billing automation tickets created in ENG backlog: one for proration algorithm (ENG-XXXX), one for credit issuance workflow (ENG-YYYY), and one for Console invoice UI changes (DES-XXX).
- Standard SQ language snippets and two supporting artifacts (sample audit log extract and KMS policy template) stored in Confluence linked from this ticket.
- Demo plan for Finance and CS showing automated credit calculation on a sandbox account with at least three edge cases covered.

Rollout plan:
1) Finalize playbook with sign-off from Finance, Legal, and Security (2 weeks).
2) Implement backend proration algorithm and credit queue (ENG sprint 2).
3) Expose "billing view" and explanation in Console with rationale and link to dispute flow (DES & Console).
4) Run pilot with 3 mid-market customers (incl. one with private deployment) for 60 days.
5) Codify SQ responses and publish artifacts for sales and enterprise intake.

Notes about SQ-specific content needed:
- Concise answer for: "How do you handle billing for mid-cycle contract changes?" -> "Redwood aligns metering to UTC invoice windows. For mid-cycle seat/commit changes we prorate usage for the remainder of the period; overages are applied as a credit on the next invoice unless immediate invoicing is contractually required." (final language to be reviewed by Legal).
- Evidence items: sample invoice diff, anonymized usage ledger for a change event, KMS key ID and retention policy doc link.

Open questions for stakeholders (actionable):
- Sales: do we allow per-customer override for immediate overage invoicing as defaultable contract term? (Decision needed)
- Legal: acceptance of UTC canonical metering for customers in non-UTC billing jurisdictions and any tax implications we should flag.
- Security: required level of detail in SQ artifacts to avoid exposing prompt-level data while providing sufficient audit trail.

Link to artifacts and references:
- Confluence playbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/billing/pm-15823-playbook (placeholder)
- ENG design doc for metering windows: https://docs.redwood.ai/eng/ENG-2764-metering-windows
- Sample invoice diff (anonymized): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/samples/invoice-diff-pm15823.pdf
- Related Linear: PM-14200 (Billing reliability initiative), ENG-2764, ENG-2910
updates: 2026-02-15 - Aisha Patel created ticket with initial scope and rationale.
2026-02-17 - Sync with Finance (R. Gomez) and Legal (T. Nguyen). Finance prefers credit-on-next-invoice by default; Legal flagged VAT/tax note for EMEA customers.
2026-02-20 - Engineering kickoff with runtime team. Agreed to expose a metering boundary flag in the usage ledger for downstream billing logic. ENG asked for explicit examples for rounding rules.

2026-02-24 - Drafted SQ language and artifact list; sent to Security (S. Blake) for review. Security requested that any exported usage ledger be aggregated at request-id level to avoid raw prompt content.

2026-02-27 - Design review: Console changes scoped to a new \"Billing adjustments\" panel showing proration math and links to dispute form. DES suggested microcopy that avoids technical terms for customers.
2026-03-01 - Updated acceptance criteria to include pilot plan and sign-offs. Next steps: Legal final language, ENG backlog PRs, pilot customer identification.

Backend endpoints for proration and credit queue implemented and covered by tests
Console UI surfaces invoice adjustments with links to dispute workflow
SQ canonical answers and two supporting artifacts uploaded to Confluence
Pilot executed with 3 customers and results documented
